pm_structure.summary: The general fund is managed in-house by iA's Investments sector under EVP & CIO Alain Bergeron, who reports to the CEO. All group investment activity - general fund (Canada and U.S.), segregated funds, iA Clarington mutual funds and oversight of external managers - sits 'under a single authority' and operates under the iA Global Asset Management (iAGAM) tradename, which is used by two legal entities: Industrial Alliance Investment Management Inc. (iAIM, the historic insurer-owned manager) and iA Global Asset Management Inc. iAGAM oversees C$156bn (Jun 30, 2026) with a dedicated general-fund team (Total Portfolio Management / liability replication) and an investment risk-monitoring team; iA Clarington is the retail fund sponsor that uses iAGAM and third-party sub-advisors. There is no external GA mandate of consequence disclosed.

rotation_commentary.text: Private fixed income: private debt corporate bonds C$5.7bn = 12% of the C$47.3bn portfolio (97% IG, North America); 'allocation has increased the portfolio efficient surface'; total portfolio risk unchanged via rebalancing.

Private credit corporate loans C$329mm (0.7% of portfolio), 100% senior secured, average quality B, 'disciplined deployment initiated in 2025', no defaults; Level 3 private FI capped at 1% of portfolio.

Asset-mix drift Jun 2025 to Jun 2026: bonds 69.0% to 64.9%, stocks 12.4% to 16.5% (part with downside protection, part pass-through UL/PAR), investment properties 3.3% to 2.9%; infrastructure & private equity 6%.

CFO Jobin (Q2 call): TPM approach minimises rate risk but keeps a small positive core-earnings sensitivity to higher long rates; 'reinvesting and lengthening the duration of our portfolio over time' adds value.
Derivatives used for yield enhancement (market index options keep equity exposure while limiting losses) in addition to seg-fund dynamic hedging and UL fund hedges.

Expected investment earnings C$499mm (+8%) helped by yield-curve steepening; GA shrank as capital was deployed into RF Capital (C$691mm) and buybacks; iA Auto Finance underwriting tightened 'a couple of years ago'.
Investment properties occupancy improved to 89.2% (Jun 2026) from 84.4% (Dec 2025); mortgage book 52% securitized/insured (down from 62%), i.e., gradual shift to uninsured/commercial mortgages.
